--- title: "2 · Data" --- ::: {.cell} ::: We demonstrate SINDy using an [APSIM simulation dataset](https://figshare.com/articles/dataset/24843705) of wheat (Bustos-Korts et al., 2019). The dataset contains daily biomass trajectories of 199 genotypes in 31 years (1983 to 2013) at Narrabri (New South Wales). The trajectories are generated by APSIM, a crop growth model, and are influenced by weather conditions, which are the same for all genotypes within a year/location. ![The data. (a) Daily temperature range in the year 1998. (b) Biomass trajectories of the 199 genotypes in that year, with the genotypes of lowest and highest final biomass and genotype g114 in colour. (c) Genotype g114 in all 31 years, with 1998 in colour: the weather differs between years, and so does the trajectory.](images/concept_data.png){width=100%} ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} wx <- read.csv("data/narrabri_weather.csv") traj <- read.csv("data/narrabri_biomass.csv.gz") head(wx, 3) head(traj, 3) ``` ::: ## Python ```python import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import numpy as np import pandas as pd from dgxe import * wx = pd.read_csv("data/narrabri_weather.csv") traj = pd.read_csv("data/narrabri_biomass.csv.gz") print(wx.head(3)) print(traj.head(3)) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` year das Tmin Tmax Rain RAD VP DL TT RAW 1 1983 15 10.0 17.0 0 12 11 11.191 247.50 0.7966 2 1983 16 3.5 15.0 0 11 10 11.180 256.75 0.7909 3 1983 17 6.0 15.5 0 13 10 11.169 267.50 0.7838 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` genotype year das biomass lai 1 g001 1983 15 0.0164 0.039 2 g001 1983 16 0.0190 0.043 3 g001 1983 17 0.0228 0.049 ``` ::: ::: ## Weather variables The weather table has one row per day and year, with the year (`year`), the days after sowing (`das`) and the following given variables. | Variable | Description | |---|---| | `Tmin`, `Tmax` | daily minimum and maximum temperature (°C) | | `Rain` | rainfall (mm) | | `RAD` | solar radiation (MJ m⁻² d⁻¹) | | `VP` | vapour pressure (hPa) | | `DL` | day length (h) | The table also contains two covariates that were constructed from these variables: `TT` and `RAW`. ## Constructed variables Two further variables in the table are constructed from the weather variables: thermal time (`TT`) and relative available water (`RAW`). ```{=html}
weather variables (given)
constructed variables
Tmin
Tmax
Rain
RAD
VP
DL
TT thermal time
\(\sum_{s \le t} \max\left(\tfrac{T_{\min,s} + T_{\max,s}}{2}, 0\right)\)
RAW relative available water
\(W_t / W_{\max}\), bucket of rain and \(\mathrm{ET}_0\)
``` Thermal time is a measure for the development of the plant, and is computed as the sum of the daily mean temperature, here with base temperature 0$^\circ$C, over the days since sowing: $$ \mathrm{TT}_t = \sum_{s \le t} \max\left(\frac{T_{\min,s} + T_{\max,s}}{2},\, 0\right). $$ Relative available water is approximated by a simple soil moisture model: rain adds water and a fraction $k$ of the reference evapotranspiration $\mathrm{ET}_0$ removes it, up to the capacity $W_{\max}$ of the soil, $$ W_t = \min\bigl(\max(W_{t-1} + P_t - k\,\mathrm{ET}_{0,t},\, 0),\, W_{\max}\bigr), \qquad \mathrm{RAW}_t = \frac{W_t}{W_{\max}}. $$ The maximum available water capacity $W_{\max} = 217.5$ mm is a property of the soil, and the initial available water $W_0 = 175$ mm is a property of the season. In this formula. Furthermore, $\mathrm{ET}_0$ is the FAO-56 Penman–Monteith reference evapotranspiration, computed from the weather variables of the table, and $k = 0.8$. So, in total we use eight variables: the six weather variables and the two constructed ones. All of them are candidates for the library. ## Variables over the years All eight variables, for all years (grey) and three selected years: ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} vars <- c("Tmin", "Tmax", "Rain", "RAD", "VP", "DL", "TT", "RAW") weather <- data.frame( year = wx$year, das = wx$das, variable = factor(rep(vars, each = nrow(wx)), vars), value = unlist(wx[vars]) ) shown <- weather[weather$year %in% c(1984, 1998, 2008), ] ggplot(weather, aes(das, value, group = year)) + geom_line(colour = "#D1D5DB", linewidth = 0.25) + geom_line(data = shown, aes(colour = factor(year)), linewidth = 0.7) + facet_wrap(~variable, scales = "free_y", nrow = 2) + scale_colour_dgxe("blue", "cyan", "burgundy") + labs(x = "days after sowing", y = NULL) + theme_dgxe() + legend_top() ``` ::: ## Python ```python VARS = ["Tmin", "Tmax", "Rain", "RAD", "VP", "DL", "TT", "RAW"] years = [1984, 1998, 2008] fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 4, figsize=(10, 4.5), sharex=True) for ax, name in zip(axes.flat, VARS): for year, g in wx.groupby("year"): ax.plot(g["das"], g[name], color=GREY, lw=0.25) for year, colour in zip(years, [BLUE, CYAN, BURGUNDY]): g = wx[wx["year"] == year] ax.plot(g["das"], g[name], color=colour, lw=0.9, label=year) ax.set_title(name, loc="left") axes[0, 0].legend(frameon=False) fig.supxlabel("days after sowing") fig.tight_layout() ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](02-data_files/figure-html/02-3-run-1.png){width=1036.8} ::: ::: ## Correlation The eight variables over all days and years, standardised. Above the diagonal: scatter plots of a random sample of 600 days. On the diagonal: the distribution of each variable (kernel density estimate). Below the diagonal: the correlation coefficient. ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} standardised <- as.data.frame(scale(wx[vars])) corr <- cor(wx[vars]) panel <- expand.grid(row = seq_along(vars), col = seq_along(vars)) label <- function(i) factor(vars[i], vars) set.seed(1) sample_days <- standardised[sample(nrow(standardised), 600), ] upper <- panel[panel$row < panel$col, ] upper <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(upper)), function(k) { i <- upper$row[k] j <- upper$col[k] data.frame( row = label(i), col = label(j), x = sample_days[[j]], y = sample_days[[i]] ) })) diagonal <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(vars), function(i) { d <- density(standardised[[i]], from = -3.5, to = 3.5, n = 200) data.frame( row = label(i), col = label(i), x = d$x, ymax = -3.5 + 6 * d$y / max(d$y) ) })) lower <- panel[panel$row > panel$col, ] lower <- data.frame( row = label(lower$row), col = label(lower$col), rho = corr[cbind(lower$row, lower$col)] ) ggplot() + geom_rect( data = lower, aes(fill = rho), xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf ) + geom_text( data = lower, aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", rho)), x = 0, y = 0, size = 2.6 ) + geom_point( data = upper, aes(x, y), size = 0.15, alpha = 0.4, colour = dgxe[["blue"]] ) + geom_ribbon( data = diagonal, aes(x, ymin = -3.5, ymax = ymax), fill = dgxe[["blue"]], alpha = 0.5 ) + facet_grid(row ~ col, switch = "y") + scale_fill_gradient2( low = dgxe[["burgundy"]], mid = "white", high = dgxe[["blue"]], limits = c(-1, 1) ) + coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-3.5, 3.5), ylim = c(-3.5, 3.5), expand = FALSE) + labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) + theme_dgxe() + theme( axis.line = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(), axis.text = element_blank(), aspect.ratio = 1, panel.spacing = unit(2, "pt"), strip.placement = "outside", strip.text = element_text(hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5, size = 11), strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5), panel.border = element_rect( colour = "#D1D5DB", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.3 ) ) ``` ::: ## Python ```python from matplotlib.colors import LinearSegmentedColormap from scipy.stats import gaussian_kde colours = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list("dgxe", [BURGUNDY, "white", BLUE]) standardised = (wx[VARS] - wx[VARS].mean()) / wx[VARS].std() corr = standardised.corr() sample = standardised.sample(600, random_state=1) grid = np.linspace(-3.5, 3.5, 200) fig, axes = plt.subplots(8, 8, figsize=(5.6, 5.6)) for i in range(8): for j in range(8): ax = axes[i, j] ax.set(xlim=(-3.5, 3.5), ylim=(-3.5, 3.5), xticks=[], yticks=[]) for spine in ax.spines.values(): spine.set(color=GREY, linewidth=0.5) if i < j: ax.scatter(sample[VARS[j]], sample[VARS[i]], s=1.5, alpha=0.4, color=BLUE, linewidths=0) elif i == j: density = gaussian_kde(standardised[VARS[i]])(grid) ax.fill_between(grid, -3.5, -3.5 + 6 * density / density.max(), color=BLUE, alpha=0.5, linewidth=0) else: rho = corr.iloc[i, j] ax.set_facecolor(colours((rho + 1) / 2)) ax.text(0, 0, f"{rho:.2f}", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=7) if i == 0: ax.set_title(VARS[j], fontsize=9, pad=3) if j == 0: ax.set_ylabel(VARS[i], rotation=0, ha="right", va="center", fontsize=9) fig.subplots_adjust(wspace=0.04, hspace=0.04) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](02-data_files/figure-html/02-5-run-1.png){width=806.4} ::: ::: We observe that many weather variables are heavily correlated. Therefore, we can expect that a library does not need all eight variables to explain the biomass trajectories. ## Response In this workshop, we focus on biomass as the trait of interest. The biomass trajectories of the 199 genotypes in four selected years are shown below. The highlighted genotypes are the ones with the lowest, median and highest final biomass in that year. ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} drv <- make_drivers(wx) tr <- make_trajectories(traj, drv) highlighted <- c("g194", "g114", "g048") # lowest, median, highest final biomass years <- traj[traj$year %in% c(1984, 1990, 1998, 2008), ] ggplot(years, aes(das, biomass, group = genotype)) + geom_line(colour = "#D1D5DB", linewidth = 0.2) + geom_line( data = years[years$genotype %in% highlighted, ], aes(colour = genotype), linewidth = 0.7 ) + facet_wrap(~year, nrow = 1) + scale_colour_dgxe("burgundy", "cyan", "blue") + labs(x = "days after sowing", y = "biomass (t/ha)") + theme_dgxe() + legend_top() ``` ::: ## Python ```python drv = make_drivers(wx) tr = make_trajectories(traj, drv) highlighted = ["g194", "g114", "g048"] # lowest, median, highest final biomass days = np.arange(tr.Y.shape[2]) + tr.das0 fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 4, sharey=True, figsize=(10, 2.8)) for ax, year in zip(axes, [1984, 1990, 1998, 2008]): i = list(tr.years).index(year) ax.plot(days, tr.Y[:, i].T, color=GREY, lw=0.2) for g, colour in zip(highlighted, [BURGUNDY, CYAN, BLUE]): ax.plot(days, tr.Y[np.searchsorted(tr.genotypes, g), i], color=colour, lw=0.9, label=g) ax.set_title(year, loc="left") axes[0].legend(frameon=False) axes[0].set_ylabel("biomass (t/ha)") fig.supxlabel("days after sowing") fig.tight_layout() ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](02-data_files/figure-html/02-4-run-1.png){width=1036.8} ::: :::
